scope: Experimental Linux x86-64 automatic xstate tracing with host native blocks and same-page direct branches; emulator-only homebrew
changes: Apply freshly decoded, bounded native blocks to ordinary host instructions as well as guest instructions.
Resolve direct same-page jumps, conditionals and loop branches from saved registers without an extra trap.
Limit branch processing to 64 branches per dispatch so native stepping and signal delivery remain possible.
Preserve real call and return stack addresses; guest callbacks continue through tracing.
limits: Experimental and off by default; game performance and compatibility have not been established.
Calls, returns, indirect or cross-page branches, RIP-relative and unsupported instructions retain native single-stepping.
No persistent block cache; concurrent unsynchronized code or permission changes are not supported.
Guest cancellation, unusual signal-mask changes, guest debugging and every possible native-to-guest callback are not validated.
Jaguar in-use tracking, unsupported host state, generated CPU-ID handling and cross-platform runtime work remain outside this change.
